content:
Today Apple released the latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, and along with the new machines, several Magic Keyboard accessories in the lineup have also received minor updates.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on keycaps, replacing them with icons instead.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio get a significant performance boost with the next-generation M6 and top-tier M5 Ultra chips.

You can now pre-order the latest models: Mac mini here, Mac Studio here.

In addition to the desktop improvements, Apple has also updated the Magic Keyboard lineup, with a subtle change on the new models.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels from most keys, replacing them with symbol icons.

Apple had earlier adopted the same approach on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and now the Magic Keyboard follows suit.

The following new Magic Keyboard models all feature this change:

  • Magic Keyboard: $99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: $149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: $179

Common keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete have changed from text to displaying only icons; on the extended model with a numeric keypad, keys such as Home, Page Up, and Page Down use new icons to replace text.

The most popular comment was posted by Caesarrr

I really cannot understand this decision. You know it will add friction for users, so what benefit is worth sacrificing the user experience?

Apart from switching to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks largely the same as the previous generation, with the same USB-C support and identical functions and layout.

If you prefer to order the new Magic Keyboard from Amazon instead of Apple, you can purchase here: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID version, Touch ID and Numeric Keypad version (black).

What do you think about the change from text labels to icons on the keyboard? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
